record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.original_question: Determine whether the set of finite finitely based completely 0-simple semigroups over Abelian groups, in particular over the two-element group, is recursive.

evidence.quote:
Problem 2.6. (G. Mashevitzky) Is the set of finite finitely based completely 0-simple semigroups
over Abelian groups, in particular, over a two-element group, recursive?
An infinite chain of varieties, generated by completely 0-simple semigroups over the two-element
group, in which finitely based and non-finitely based varieties alternate, was constructed in [11].

          In the following series of problems we consider varieties of ordered semigroups, that is,
semigroups equipped with a partial order compatible with the semigroup operation. Such varieties
are defined by identities together with identical inequalities. Identical inequalities are often called
identical relations of precedence. For example, the semigroup of real numbers on the segment
S = [0, 1] with multiplication satisfies the identical inequality xy ≤ x.
          E.S. Lyapin proposed the problem of studying varieties defined by identities and identical
inequalities in the late 1970s.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A semigroup $S$ with zero $0$ is called completely $0$-simple if $S^2 \neq \{0\}$, $S$ has no proper two-sided ideals other than $\{0\}$, and $S$ contains a $0$-minimal left ideal and a $0$-minimal right ideal. By the Rees theorem, every finite completely $0$-simple semigroup is isomorphic to a Rees matrix semigroup $\mathcal{M}^0(G; I, \Lambda; P)$ over a finite group $G$ with a regular sandwich matrix $P$ over $G \cup \{0\}$.

A semigroup is said to be finitely based if the variety it generates can be defined by finitely many identities (i.e., its identities admit a finite basis).

Identifying finite completely $0$-simple semigroups over Abelian groups with their finite descriptions as Rees matrix semigroups $\mathcal{M}^0(A; I, \Lambda; P)$ where $A$ is a finite Abelian group, decide whether the set of (codes of) finite finitely based completely $0$-simple semigroups over finite Abelian groups is a recursive (decidable) subset. Treat in particular the special case where $A$ is the two-element group $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$: is the set of finite finitely based completely $0$-simple semigroups of the form $\mathcal{M}^0(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}; I, \Lambda; P)$ recursive?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent collection of unsolved problems in semigroup theory and is attributed to G. Mashevitzky. A related construction (an infinite alternating chain of finitely based / non-finitely based varieties generated by completely 0-simple semigroups over the two-element group) is known, but no decision procedure determining recursiveness of the set has been established. Searches did not turn up a published resolution.
